newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CULVERHOUSE SENDING OFF MAKES CUP HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CULVERHOUSE SENDING OFF MAKES CUP HISTORY.

text.p: Swindon's Ian Culverhouse made F.A. Cup history when he was sent off after just 52 seconds in his side's 3-0 third round defeat at Everton on Sunday.
Culverhouse's dismissal, for deliberate handball in the penalty area, was the fastest in the 126-year history of England's premier cup competition.
It resulted in a penalty, converted by Ukrainian Andrei Kanchelskis.
Everton, Cup winners in 1995, increased their lead after 17 minutes following an error by former Liverpool winger Mark Walters.
His backpass was woefully short allowing England forward Nick Barmby to intercept, round goalkeeper Fraser Digby and score.
Duncan Ferguson made it 3-0 early in the second half, rising above the Swindon defence to head home a cross from Earl Barrett.
Swindon's miserable afternoon was completed when Gary Elkins was sent off after 74 minutes for a second bookable offence.
Earlier in the day, England midfielder Robert Lee scored against his former club Charlton before the first division side fought back to draw 1-1 with Newcastle.
Lee, who played over 300 times for the Londoners before signing for Kevin Keegan's side four years ago, put Newcastle ahead after 33 minutes with a fortuitous goal.

Lee Clark crossed from the right and Alan Shearer rose at the far post to head the ball to Lee, who fluffed his first attempt completely -- inadvertently wrong-footing his marker -- before poking the ball into the net from eight metres.
Minutes earlier, first division Charlton had had what appeared to be legitimate appeals for a penalty turned down.
Paul Sturgess centred from the left to England under-21 forward Shaun Newton, who bustled past John Beresford only to be clearly hauled back by his shirt as he geared up for a shot.
The referee waved play on and within five minutes Newcastle were in front.
The premier league side, six times winners of the Cup, looked to be heading for the fourth round until 12 minutes from time when Mark Kinsella scored a stunning equaliser.
Picking the ball up in midfield, he strode forward and cracked a right-foot shot into the right-hand side of Shaka Hislop's net from 25 metres.
"It would have been (a perfect homecoming) but Charlton played really well and deserved their draw," said Lee, who will miss the replay at St James' Park due to suspension.
